answer_text:
Assume \(f\) is sufficiently smooth near \(0\). Write its Taylor expansion as

\[
f(x)=f(0)+f'(0)x+\frac{f''(0)}2x^2+\frac{f'''(0)}6x^3+O(x^4).
\]

Then

\[
\int_0^h f(x)\,dx
= f(0)h+\frac{f'(0)}2h^2+\frac{f''(0)}6h^3+\frac{f'''(0)}{24}h^4+O(h^5).
\]

Also,

\[
f(0)=f(0),
\]

\[
f\left(\frac h3\right)
=f(0)+f'(0)\frac h3+\frac{f''(0)}2\left(\frac h3\right)^2
+\frac{f'''(0)}6\left(\frac h3\right)^3+O(h^4),
\]

so

\[
f\left(\frac h3\right)
=f(0)+\frac{f'(0)}3h+\frac{f''(0)}{18}h^2+\frac{f'''(0)}{162}h^3+O(h^4).
\]

Similarly,

\[
f(h)=f(0)+f'(0)h+\frac{f''(0)}2h^2+\frac{f'''(0)}6h^3+O(h^4).
\]

Thus

\[
h\left(af(0)+bf\left(\frac h3\right)+cf(h)\right)
\]

\[
=(a+b+c)f(0)h+\left(\frac b3+c\right)f'(0)h^2
+\left(\frac b{18}+\frac c2\right)f''(0)h^3
+\left(\frac b{162}+\frac c6\right)f'''(0)h^4+O(h^5).
\]

Therefore the numerator is

\[
\begin{aligned}
&\int_0^h f(x)\,dx-h\left(af(0)+bf\left(\frac h3\right)+cf(h)\right)\\
&=\bigl(1-a-b-c\bigr)f(0)h\\
&\quad+\left(\frac12-\frac b3-c\right)f'(0)h^2\\
&\quad+\left(\frac16-\frac b{18}-\frac c2\right)f''(0)h^3\\
&\quad+\left(\frac1{24}-\frac b{162}-\frac c6\right)f'''(0)h^4+O(h^5).
\end{aligned}
\]

For

\[
\frac{\int_0^h f(x)\,dx-h\left(af(0)+bf\left(\frac h3\right)+cf(h)\right)}{h^4}
\]

to have a finite nonzero limit, the coefficients of \(h,h^2,h^3\) must vanish. Hence

\[
a+b+c=1,
\]

\[
\frac b3+c=\frac12,
\]

\[
\frac b{18}+\frac c2=\frac16.
\]

From the second equation,

\[
b+3c=\frac32.
\]

From the third equation,

\[
b+9c=3.
\]

Subtracting gives

\[
6c=\frac32 \implies c=\frac14.
\]

Then

\[
b=3-9c=3-\frac94=\frac34,
\]

and

\[
a=1-b-c=1-\frac34-\frac14=0.
\]

Now compute

\[
a+2b+3c
=0+2\left(\frac34\right)+3\left(\frac14\right)
=\frac32+\frac34
=\frac94.
\]

Thus

\[
\boxed{\frac94}
\]
